newsitem.title: USA: Holocaust survivors to get Nazi gold.
newsitem.headline: Holocaust survivors to get Nazi gold.

text.p: Six tons of looted Nazi gold that was to have been distributed to the central banks of Europe will instead go to individual Holocaust survivors, sources close to the negotiations said on Wednesday.
The sources, who asked not to be identified, said they expected the decision to be approved formally at a two-day 25-nation conference to be held in London in December.

The six tons of gold, worth $68 million, are the last of 377 tons captured by the Allies from the Nazis at the end of the Second World War. Two tons are stored at the Federal Reserve Bank in New York and four tons at the Bank of England in London.

In order for Holocaust survivors to get the gold, at least a dozen nations of Europe must forego their claims -- including France, Austria, Slovakia, Greece, Croatia, the Netherlands, Poland, Belgium and the Czech Republic.

Since the end of the war, a commission set up by Britain, France and the United States has distributed 371 tons of gold, worth close to $4 billion, to European nations whose treasuries were looted by the Nazis.

Last May a U.S. government task force headed by then Commerce Department Undersecretary Stuart Eizenstat concluded that the looted gold which had previously been deemed to have come only from central banks actually included gold from individual Holocaust victims.

The Nazis were meticulous and brutal in their quest for gold, going so far as to rip the the gold teeth from death camp victims for smelting into gold ingots that were then sold abroard, including to neutral Switzerland.

The United States recommended that the remaining six tons of gold be distributed to benefit Holocaust survivors, as they were excluded from previous allocations of the looted gold which went only to European central banks.

After the Eizenstat report was published, World Jewish Congress President Edgar Bronfman wrote the foreign ministers of European nations asking that they voluntarily give up claims to the remaining gold under moral obligation.
The WJC said it has received both formal and informal assurances from the countries involved that they would give up their claims and support distribution of the gold to Holocaust survivors.

Meanwhile, sources close to the negotiations said that at the prompting of Britain, France, and the United States, the European countries are expected to use the coming London conference to announce their agreement to the plan.
The WJC released letters of support from four European governments for the initiative.

The Greek government said that "within a defined period of time, (the gold) should be distributed to individual survivors of Nazi concentration camps and part of it should be used to benefit direct descendants of Holocaust victims."
Austrian Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schussel said the gold "should be made available to individual survivors of Nazi persecution through the establishment of a fund."
Similiar letters of support came from the governments of Slovakia and Croatia.
British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook announced plans for the conference in London on Wednesday, saying it would look into compensation for individual victims of Nazi persecution.
